title: Embracing high clock frequency alongside complex design
decision: Opted to also embrace the speed-demon (high clock rate) approach while retaining complex high-IPC design elements.
alternatives_or_rejected: Remaining solely in the traditional IBM UNIX 'braniac' camp that emphasized higher instructions-per-cycle over high clock rate.
rationale: To maintain leadership position and deliver best-of-breed operating frequencies; the design was introduced at 1.1–1.3 GHz and surpassed other 64-bit microprocessors on key benchmarks.
outcome: High-frequency operation together with superscalar out-of-order execution capable of up to eight-issue and sustained five-instruction completion.
weakest_point: Exact introductory frequency numbers (1.1/1.3 GHz) may be recalled with slight imprecision.

title: RAS philosophy beyond ECC and reliable parts
where_in_paper: Guiding principles (Leadership in reliability, availability, and serviceability)
decision: Require an approach that eliminates outages and provides redundancy where errors cannot be eliminated; transform hard machine stops (checkstops) into synchronous machine interrupts to software where possible.
alternatives_or_rejected: Achieving high reliability only by choosing reliable parts and incorporating ECC into major arrays.
rationale: Servers have evolved toward continuous operation; outages of any kind are not tolerated; build on mainframe-like RAS attributes already being introduced.
outcome: Pervasive RAS features integrated throughout the system (further detailed in a companion paper).
weakest_point: Precise wording of the 'transform checkstops' clause.

title: Full-system co-design from the outset
decision: Begin with the full design in mind; design the entire system together from processor to memory and I/O bridge chips; treat POWER4 as an architecture for interconnecting chips, not merely a chip.
alternatives_or_rejected: Designing the processor in isolation and later attaching a subsystem.
rationale: A new high-performance processor needs a new subsystem to feed it effectively; marriage of process technology, packaging, and microarchitecture allows software to exploit the whole system.
outcome: Distributed-switch interconnect supporting up to 32-way SMP; buses that scale with processor frequency to preserve balance.
weakest_point: Exact description of the interconnect topology name ('distributed switch').

title: Single design addressing both technical and commercial workloads
where_in_paper: Guiding principles (Balanced technical and commercial performance)
decision: A single design satisfying both high-bandwidth technical/HPC requirements and commercial data-sharing/SMP-scaling requirements, supporting both pSeries and iSeries.
alternatives_or_rejected: Separate designs optimized only for technical (prior POWER3 lineage) or only for commercial (prior RS64 lineage).
rationale: As e-business evolves, data-intensive and commercial demands merge; one design meets both pSeries and iSeries needs.
outcome: POWER4 used across both commercial and technical systems while remaining binary-compatible with prior PowerPC/PowerPC AS software.
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly names the prior RS64/POWER3 split as the rejected alternative.

title: Dual-core chip with shared L2 and frequency-scalable fabric
where_in_paper: POWER4 chip section and system interconnect discussion
decision: Place two identical processors on one chip sharing a unified L2 via a CIU crossbar; implement a scalable chip-to-chip and MCM-to-MCM fabric whose buses run at fractions of processor frequency and scale with it.
alternatives_or_rejected: Treating POWER4 solely as a single-processor chip; fixed-frequency system buses that would unbalance as processor frequency rose.
rationale: SMP optimization for high-throughput multitasking; preserve system balance as technology improves frequencies; leverage packaging (four chips per module, four modules for 32-way).
outcome: 174-million-transistor chip presenting a two-way SMP to software; systems up to 32-way with balanced bandwidth.
weakest_point: Exact bus-width and frequency-ratio numbers (e.g., 2:1, 3:1) may mix paper text with general recollection.
